name: novel_truthy_asyncmock
transcript:
assistant: `tests/test_dispatcher.py::test_drain_until_empty` hangs under CI. The loop is `while queue_probe(): await drain_one()`. In the test `queue_probe` is a bare `AsyncMock()`; every call returns a new AsyncMock, which is always truthy, so the `while` condition is never falsy and `drain_one()` is awaited forever.
assistant: Fix: give the mock a concrete side effect — `probe = AsyncMock(side_effect=[True, True, False])` — so the guard actually goes falsy. The production guard also now compares `probe_result.depth > 0` instead of relying on truthiness. Test completes immediately.
tool_result: pytest tests/test_dispatcher.py::test_drain_until_empty -q -> 1 passed in 0.12s
assistant: Root cause — a bare AsyncMock stood in for a boolean probe; because every AsyncMock is truthy the drain loop never terminated. General fix: assert on a concrete attribute/return value, never on the raw mock's truthiness.

known_patterns.description: An unbounded `await proc.communicate()` on a long-lived subprocess blocks the async cycle until the watchdog fires.
Asserting on a created task before `await asyncio.sleep(0)` sees stale state because the task never got a chance to run.

notes: Root cause = a bare AsyncMock is always truthy, so a while-guard never terminates. Distinct from the subprocess and sleep(0) patterns known, so novel is expected; a faithful pattern names AsyncMock and its truthiness.
